# Exact-head CI and merge-queue observations

Swarm CI Monitor records all available check-run pages for the selected PR head
and marks the observation incomplete when pagination or revision identity cannot
be verified. A known merge-queue run can be recorded separately with its own SHA
and status. Terminal merge reporting requires the PR's merge commit and
independent Git evidence on the target base.

The monitor still uses the repository's required-check and merge authorization
rules. MCP-only hosts need a paginated check-run read and independent Git proof
for the corresponding observations.
<!-- custom-release-notes:end -->

# Verify release reviews and trace evidence

Release-bound issue traces schedule native Swarm review for the exact pull request head. Merge admission verifies the native submission receipt against GitHub and blocks stale, incomplete, or altered review evidence. Review lanes return partial coverage when the host budget is exhausted.

Checkpoint freezing also generates a base replay and test inventory. New trace checks verify published acceptance commands, checkpoint receipts, and the squash patch against the reviewed change.

# Coder committed output no longer wedges reviewer dispatch; swarm_memory tools honor the enabled flag

## What

Two shared-root workflow fixes:

- A coder delegation whose declared output was committed, left uncommitted, or
  otherwise missed guardrail write-routing now reaches the reviewer gate (in
  git workspaces; a workspace where git is permanently unavailable still
  cannot dispatch the reviewer, but it now denies with a typed terminal code
  instead of looping — `no_git_workspace`, `git_unavailable`,
  `git_dubious_ownership` or `git_unhealthy`, all `retryable=false`, per the
  #3680 change in this same release; only transient causes such as an unborn
  HEAD keep the retryable `head_timeout` arm) and guardrail-routed
  completions now proceed when the git channel is merely degraded, e.g. the
  coder dispatched into a repo before its first commit. At
  every coder completion whose declared scope still has unrouted files, the
  reviewer-scope generation reconciles declared-scope changes from two sources
  — the committed diff since the dispatch-time HEAD and the declared-scope
  working tree — routing each with its fingerprint. Reconciliation is
  path-base correct for workspaces whose project root is a subdirectory of
  the git repository (paths are normalized to the project root, so monorepo
  layouts attribute correctly). The capture prefix is resolved by git itself
  (`rev-parse --show-prefix`), never lexically — on hosts whose temp paths
  surface Windows 8.3 short names (`RUNNER~1`), a lexical `path.relative`
  against the canonical `rev-parse --show-toplevel` output treated the two
  spellings as different directories and misclassified every working-tree
  change as outside the project root (declared-scope output silently left
  the reviewer gate; no-change workspaces read dirty). Output that
  guardrail routing never observed
  no longer strands the generation and throws terminal
  `REVIEWER_SCOPE_STALE (retryable=false)`.
- Attribution problems now surface typed, actionable denials instead of one
  terminal code. A generation with no routed writes and no provable committed
  change denies reviewer dispatch with `REVIEWER_ATTRIBUTION_EMPTY`
  (retryable=true). Routed files with incomplete fingerprints deny with
  `REVIEWER_CAPTURE_INCOMPLETE` (retryable, re-dispatch the coder) or, for
  permanent capture failures, `REVIEWER_CAPTURE_FAILED` with a repair-then-
  re-dispatch-the-coder action (the collecting-state denial sanitizes the
  failure file before interpolation). Declared-scope change sets exceeding the 256-file generation cap are
  refused up front with a `REVIEWER_SCOPE_GENERATION_OVERFLOW` advisory
  instead of silently destroying the generation. Genuine post-capture drift on
  a ready generation remains terminal `REVIEWER_SCOPE_STALE` and now states
  `retryable=false` in its own text.
- The no-change verdict is runtime-aware, scope-truthful, and per-file:
  plugin-owned `.swarm/` dirt no longer flips a truthful no-change completion
  into a guardrail-bypass suspicion (including wholly untracked `.swarm/`
  directories, now enumerated per file), `REVIEWER_SCOPE_NO_CHANGE` says "no
  committed or working-tree change exists within the declared reviewer scope"
  instead of claiming a globally empty workspace diff, and the verdict is
  path-base correct in subdirectory project roots. A clean working tree whose
  committed diff cannot be proven is

# Fragment-gate hardening: byte-strict decoding, aggregator parity, argv strictness, test hygiene

## What

- `scripts/check-pending-fragment.ts` now decodes list inputs byte-strictly:
  invalid UTF-8 (file or stdin) and NUL bytes inside newline-framed input
  exit 2 with no verdict instead of silently classifying replacement
  characters or a glued blob as one path (#3306 AC1/AC2).
- `isPendingFragment` (`scripts/user-visible-paths.ts`) matches the release
  aggregator's name rules: C0 control characters, `..` segments,
  leading-`./` forms, and any backslash-bearing name (the aggregator's
  collection path cannot resolve the normalized form, so a root-level
  backslash-named file would pass the gate yet ship no release note) no
  longer satisfy the fragment mandate, and
  the `.md` suffix matches case-insensitively, so a `X.MD` fragment that the
  release pipeline would collect is no longer rejected by the gate (#3306
  AC3/AC4). The pull_request display in `pr-standards.yml` matches `.MD`
  fragments too, and its `localWorkflowHashes` pin is refreshed in the same
  change.
- A stat-able but unreadable list file now exits 2 through the usage-error
  path instead of an uncaught stack trace (#3306 AC5; new
  `_internals.readFileSync` seam + exported `readBoundedFileSync`).
- A `--`-prefixed token after a value-taking option is a usage error, and
  direct `--added` values are decoded under the selected framing with
  exactly-one-path cardinality (empty, multi-record, and separator-bearing
  values exit 2) (#3306 AC6/AC7).
- Matched fragment names and visible paths are rendered with every control
  byte (C0 and DEL) in explicit `\xNN` form in gate messages (#3361 AC4
  escaping arm).
- Test hygiene: the transport suite removes every temp directory it creates
  (exact-list `afterAll`), and every test that parsed YAML through the
  transitively-resolved `yaml` package now imports the declared `js-yaml`
  instead (#3308 AC4/AC5; the release-owner guard forbids non-release PRs
  from editing package.json, so declaring `yaml` itself is not possible
  here). New pre-authored battery
  `tests/unit/scripts/check-pending-fragment-strictness-3306-3308-3361.test.ts`
  pins the one-listing invariant, the jsonl lone-record fixture, the
  `--paths-format` enum branch, the argv→source matrix, the pull_request
  arm's empty-changed exit, and the uppercase-`.MD` display.

## Why

The gate and the release aggregator disagreed about which names count as
pending fragments, malformed lists could produce a verdict instead of exit
2, and several load-bearing behaviors (one gh listing per dispatch,
jsonl-newline handling, the enum branch, the empty-changed exit) shipped
with no discriminating test — a regression in any of them would have stayed
green.

## Verification

17 frozen acceptance checks (9 DISCRIMINATING RED→GREEN, 6 PRESERVING
GREEN→GREEN, battery-integrity NEW-SURFACE + its C5 seam row): all PASS at the
shipped head (battery: 27 pass + 1 by-design POSIX-only skip);
15-suite fragment-gate battery 256 tests, 255 pass + 1 by-design POSIX-only
skip, 0 fail; typecheck, biome ci, check:test-tmpdir, check:test-clock,
check:mock-cleanup, required-check-contract green.

## Migration

No workflow changes needed for well-formed inputs; every strictness change
fires on inputs that are malformed (invalid UTF-8, NUL-in-newline, flag-like
values, multi-record argv values) or on names the release pipeline cannot
actually collect (backslash/dotdot/dot-slash-prefixed fragment names). Two
classes deserve explicit mention: a repository path that is not valid UTF-8
(legal on POSIX filesystems) now fails the gate closed through the
infrastructure envelope instead of classifying with substituted characters,
and a direct `--added` value under the legacy newline framing tolerates
leading/trailing line separators (embedded separators are refused).

# Fix: shell write/destructive gates judge awk programs, xargs-fed verbs, sudoedit, shred, chroot roots, paren-led login sudo, and GNU-time payloads (#3648, #3652 items 2-4 + dispositions)

Seven previously admitted write/delete-gate bypass spellings now deny, the
same-family residuals from #3652 get pinned dispositions, and the planted-link
redaction in authority denials gains its first test pin:

- **awk/gawk/mawk/nawk/original-awk inline programs**
  (`awk 'BEGIN{print > "../secret"}'`, `awk 'BEGIN{system("rm -rf ../x")}'`)
  now classify as interpreter evals — exact `python -c`/`perl -e` parity.
  `awk -f progfile data` keeps the script-file carve-out, and
  `awk -i inplace <clean-program> <operand>` keeps the in-place carve-out —
  the carve-out applies ONLY when the program text carries no output
  redirection, pipe, `system(…)` or `getline` (an `-i inplace` edit whose
  program also writes elsewhere classifies as an eval; `-i inplace` does not
  disable `print >` — verified against real gawk). DISCLOSED over-deny: every
  inline awk program — including benign `awk '{print}'` — is judged as an eval
  under a declared scope (same contract as `python3 -c 'print(1)'` today);
  run from an in-scope cwd it admits.
- **xargs-fed delete/write verbs** (`echo ../x | xargs rm -rf`, `xargs rm -rf`,
  `find .. | xargs rm -rf`, `xargs -I{} cp src/a {}`) withdraw fail-closed —
  stdin-supplied targets are statically unknowable. The verb position is
  CLASSIFIED, not just table-matched: an interpreter/shell verb
  (`xargs sh -c 'rm -rf ../secret'`, `xargs python3 -c …`,
  `echo x | xargs awk 'BEGIN{print > "…"}'`), a launcher verb
  (`xargs env rm …`), a nested `xargs`, or an expansion-bearing verb
  (`xargs "$CMD" …`) withdraws too, and the walk anchors on the
  wrapper-consumed tail so group-wrapped forms (`(sudo xargs cp …)`) deny.
  DISCLOSED over-deny: with an UNKNOWN xargs option the verb position is
  unknowable and any write-verb word in the remaining words triggers the
  withdrawal.
- **`sudoedit`** is recognized as an edit form with its documented option
  synopsis; `sudoedit ../secret.txt` denies. `sudoedit -h HOST` edits on a
  remote host — every operand withdraws (landing unmodeled). `sudoedit -R DIR`
  withdraws relative operands (chroot base unresolvable for edits).
- **`shred`** operands are overwrite write-targets (`shred ../x` denies,
  `shred src/a` admits under scope `src/`), with the documented GNU grammar
  (`--remove[=how]` glued value; detached words stay operands; numeric
  filenames after `--` are real operands).
- **`sudo --chroot`/`-R DIR`** re-bases the wrapped tail: relative operands
  are judged under the chroot root (`sudo --chroot ../X cp a src/esc.txt`
  denies), and any tail containing an absolute write spelling (including
  embedded `dd of=/abs` targets) withdraws whole-tail — DISCLOSED over-deny:
  legitimate in-chroot absolute writes deny too. Repeated `-R` is a sudo
  usage error and denies. Wrapper-owned outer redirects
  (`sudo --chroot /r true > src/ok.txt`) stay judged at the invoking cwd.
- **Parenthesized login sudo** (`( sudo -i sh -c 'cd src && rm -rf x' )`,
  glued **argument-free** `(sudo -i`/`((sudo -i`/`{sudo -i;}` — including the
  nested standalone+glued forms and the stdin-fed pipe of the argument-free
  form, `echo … | (sudo -i)`, brace groups) no longer escapes the login-shell
  withdrawal; `>(cat)`/`2>(wc)` redirect openers are untouched. DISCLOSED
  pre-existing residual: glued forms carrying a command argument
  (`echo … | (sudo -s sh)`) remain admitted (base-class gap tracked in #3688).
- **GNU `time` payloads** are analyzed: `time -o src/t.txt sh -c "echo x >
  ../y.txt"` denies (bare keyword and GNU spellings) for WRITE payloads, and
  time-masked RECURSIVE DELETES deny under the default config too

# Verification-surface gates: battery admission proof, recurrence-table generator, cluster preflight, cost/yield ledger, PR-body order check, gate-state parity ratchet

## What

Closes seven verification/process gaps surfaced by the PR #3593 retrospective (#3605) and the local-gate subset gap (#3601), each by an executing check instead of orchestrator discipline: a fail-closed multi-file battery wrapper (`scripts/ci/run-test-battery.ts` — refuses unmatched paths that raw `bun test` batches silently drop, propagates failures, asserts discovered == executed, records a tree receipt); a merge-queue-readiness tree-receipt checker (`scripts/ci/check-battery-tree-receipt.sh` + protocol wiring) that refuses a battery whose recorded tree is not the tree it must validate; a fail-closed Phase 4.2 disposition-table generator (`.opencode/skills/issue-tracer/scripts/generate-recurrence-table.sh` — unmatched joins, digest disagreement, and count drift become refusals); a recorded cluster-preflight artifact required by `trace-check.sh phase 1` (per-candidate claim + open-PR evidence; issue-tracer v3.0.3); a per-lane cost/yield ledger for broad reviews (`.opencode/skills/swarm-pr-review/scripts/cost-yield-ledger.sh` + Phase 9 step + harness-recovery reference; cost and yield are paired per row); a local PR-body section-ORDER gate mirror (`scripts/check-publication-body-order.sh` wired into the publication gate); and a one-directional `PrWorkflowGateStateSchema` → `PrWorkflowGateState` shape-parity ratchet (AST-based; fails closed on unsupported declaration shapes). Also re-anchors three stale prose citations and bumps the issue-tracer (201→202) and swarm-pr-review (1716→1717) progressive-disclosure baselines with justification.

Migration note: the cluster-preflight requirement makes `trace-check.sh phase 1` refuse traces created before issue-tracer v3.0.3 that lack `repro/cluster-preflight.md`; record the preflight artifact (template in `references/phase-0-setup.md`) before re-running phase 1 on such a trace.

## Why

During the PR #3593 cycle a pin battery invoked a wrong-directory path, bun silently ran the remaining files, the recorded pass was vacuous, and CI's virtual-merge run caught it ~40 minutes later; the Phase 4.2 table pipeline fell back silently on unmatched joins and consumed two critic rounds; cluster selection spent ~15 minutes of setup on issues a parallel session had claimed; the local publication gate passed a wrongly-ordered PR body that the remote pr-standards check then failed; and a schema/interface divergence produced 15 CI-invisible TS2339 errors in test files. Each failure mode was enforced only by orchestrator vigilance; each is now a local, fail-closed check (issues #3605, #3601).
<!-- custom-release-notes:end -->
